passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations should be read together with TD Group’s consolidated financial statements and the related notes included elsewhere in this report. The following discussion may contain predictions, estimates and other forward-looking statements that involve a number of risks and uncertainties, including those discussed under the heading entitled “Risk Factors” included elsewhere in this report. These risks could cause our actual results to differ materially from any future performance suggested below. Overview We believe we are a leading global designer, producer and supplier of highly engineered proprietary aerospace components with significant aftermarket content. We seek to develop highly customized products to solve specific needs for aircraft operators and manufacturers. We attempt to differentiate ourselves based on engineering, service and manufacturing capabilities. We believe that our products have strong brand names within the industry and that we have a reputation for high quality, reliability and strong customer support. We believe we have achieved steady, long-term growth in sales and improvements in operating performance due to our competitive strengths and through execution of our value-driven operating strategy. More specifically, focusing our businesses on our value-driven operating strategy of obtaining profitable new business, carefully controlling the cost structure via productivity and cost improvements and pricing our highly engineered value-added products to fairly reflect the value we provide and the resources required to do so has historically resulted in improvements in gross profit and income from operations over the long-term. We maintain a disciplined acquisition strategy focused on proprietary commercial aerospace component businesses with significant aftermarket content, where we see a clear path to create value and earn private equity-like returns by applying our three core value drivers. Integrating acquired businesses into our existing operations and applying our operating strategy has historically improved the financial performance of the acquired businesses. For fiscal year 2026, we generated net sales of $10,557 million, gross profit of $6,254 million or 59.2% of net sales, and net income attributable to TD Group of $2,107 million. Our commercial aftermarket sales are primarily a function of air travel demand. Commercial aftermarket sales increased in fiscal 2026 compared to fiscal 2025 primarily due to overall demand, which resulted in higher flight hours and utilization of passenger and freight aircraft, despite the softening in industry capacity and RPKs arising from the conflict in the Middle East. Sales also benefited from customers completing deferred maintenance work. We are monitoring the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and the adverse effects on global energy supplies and prices, global supply chains and commercial air travel. To date, we have not seen a significant change in commercial aftermarket order activity relative to the levels prior to the start of the conflict, as demand remains strong. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Below are material risks and uncertainties that could negatively affect our business and financial condition and could cause our actual results to differ materially from those expressed in forward-looking statements contained in this report. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations and financial condition. You should not interpret the disclosure of any risk factor to imply that the risk has not already materialized. Risks Related to our Strategy Our business focuses almost exclusively on the aerospace and defense industry. A period of significant market disruption in the aerospace and defense industry, or other macroeconomic factors, may disproportionately disrupt our business compared to more diversified peer companies. We may rely heavily on certain customers for much of our sales. Our top ten customers for fiscal year 2026 accounted for approximately 45% of our net sales. A material reduction in purchasing by one of our larger customers for any reason, including but not limited to general economic or aerospace downturns, decreased production, strike or resourcing, could have a material adverse effect on results of operations, financial position and cash flows. We generally do not have guaranteed future sales of our products. Further, when we enter into fixed price contracts with some of our customers, we take the risk for cost overruns. As is customary in our business, we do not generally have long-term contracts with most of our aftermarket customers and, therefore, do not have guaranteed future sales. Although we have long-term contracts with many of our OEM customers, many of those customers may terminate the contracts on short notice and, in most cases, our customers have not committed to buy any minimum quantity of our products. In addition, in certain cases, we must anticipate the future volume of orders based upon the historic purchasing patterns of customers and upon our discussions with customers as to their anticipated future requirements, and this anticipated future volume of orders may not materialize. We also have entered into multi-year, fixed-price contracts with some of our customers, pursuant to which we have agreed to perform the work at a fixed price and, accordingly, realize all the benefit or detriment resulting from any decreases or increases in the costs of making these products. This risk is greater in a high inflationary environment. Sometimes we accept a fixed-price contract for a product that we have not previously produced, and this may increase the risk of cost overruns or delays in the completion of the design and manufacturing of the product. Most of our contracts do not permit us to recover increases in raw material prices, taxes or labor costs. Furthermore, entering into fixed-price contracts with the United States Government (“U.S. Government”), particularly for small-quantity or spot purchases made without reliable forecasts, exposes us to the risk of cost overruns and reduced margins if production costs increase or economies of scale cannot be achieved. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin is far above the sector median, reflecting proprietary aerospace components and significant aftermarket content that carries pricing power. This earnings quality underpins cash generation even as the balance sheet carries heavy leverage, and it is the main offset to the weak coverage metrics noted below.

Liquidity is comfortable: the current ratio sits well above the sector median and above one, with current assets covering near-term obligations. Cash balances provide a modest buffer, though the bulk of liquidity is working capital rather than discretionary cash for debt reduction.

key_risks.text: Leverage is the central concern: gross and net leverage sit far above the sector median, and net leverage rose year over year as debt growth outpaced EBITDA. The indicative profile is highly leveraged, and the upgrade threshold remains distant, so deleveraging depends on sustained EBITDA growth rather than organic cash sweep.

Customer concentration is a concrete disclosed risk: the top ten customers account for roughly forty-five percent of net sales, and most aftermarket customers have no long-term contracts or minimum quantities. Loss of a major OEM or aftermarket account, or fixed-price cost overruns, would hit revenue and margins disproportionately versus diversified peers.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is weak relative to peers and declined year over year, with operating income covering interest only modestly. Cash interest paid is used as the cost proxy, so coverage is measured on a cash basis; the thin cushion leaves little room for rate resets or EBITDA slippage before coverage deteriorates further.

Free cash flow covers dividends many times over but falls short of buybacks and total shareholder distributions, meaning repurchases are partly debt-funded. Cash flow to debt is far below the sector median and slipped year over year, so debt service relies on refinancing access rather than internally generated repayment capacity.

overall_credit_view.text: The maturity profile is the key refinancing consideration: the bulk of long-term debt falls due beyond year five, but sizeable tranches concentrate in years three through five. Near-term maturities are modest, giving time to refinance, yet the heavy back-end load leaves the issuer exposed to market access at each refinancing window.

Overall, TDG is a high-margin, cash-generative aerospace supplier whose leverage and coverage sit well outside sector norms, placing it in the highly leveraged band. Deleveraging is plausible through EBITDA growth, but buybacks exceeding free cash flow and concentrated customer exposure keep the credit view cautious pending sustained debt reduction.

credit_strengths.text: 營運利潤率遠高於行業中位數，反映專有航空航天零部件及具定價能力的重大售後市場內容。此盈利質量支撐現金生成，即使資產負債表背負沉重槓桿，亦是下文所述疲弱覆蓋指標的主要抵銷因素。
流動性充裕：流動比率遠高於行業中位數且高於一，流動資產覆蓋短期債務。現金結餘提供適度緩衝，惟大部分流動性屬營運資金而非可用於減債的可自由支配現金。

key_risks.text: 槓桿為核心憂慮：總槓桿及淨槓桿遠高於行業中位數，且淨槓桿按年上升，因債務增長快於EBITDA。指示性狀況為高度槓桿，升級門檻仍然遙遠，故去槓桿取決於持續EBITDA增長而非自然現金清償。
客戶集中為具體披露風險：前十大客戶約佔淨銷售額百分之四十五，且大部分售後市場客戶並無長期合約或最低採購量。失去主要OEM或售後市場客戶，或固定價格成本超支，將對收入及利潤率造成較多元化同業更不成比例的衝擊。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋相對同業疲弱且按年下降，營運收入僅勉強覆蓋利息。現金利息支出用作成本代理，故覆蓋以現金基礎計量；緩衝薄弱，利率重設或EBITDA下滑的空間有限，覆蓋將進一步惡化。
自由現金流覆蓋股息多倍，但不足以覆蓋回購及股東分派總額，意味回購部分由債務融資。現金流對債務比率遠低於行業中位數且按年下滑，故償債依賴再融資渠道而非內部產生還款能力。

overall_credit_view.text: 到期結構為關鍵再融資考量：大部分長期債務於五年後到期，但可觀批次集中於第三至第五年。近期到期規模適中，提供再融資時間，惟沉重的後端負荷使發行人於每個再融資窗口面臨市場准入風險。
整體而言，TDG為高利潤率、現金生成的航空航天供應商，其槓桿及覆蓋遠離行業常態，使其處於高度槓桿區間。透過EBITDA增長去槓桿屬可行，惟回購超出自由現金流及客戶集中風險使信貸觀點保持審慎，直至持續減債。
